profiles.name: Isaac Antonio Villegas Molina
profiles.description:
Isaac Antonio Villegas Molina is a Los Angeles day laborer and a named plaintiff in Vasquez-Perdomo v. Noem, the Southern California civil-rights lawsuit alleging that the Department of Homeland Security has unconstitutionally arrested and detained Latino day laborers, bus-stop riders, and street vendors to meet arbitrary arrest quotas without reasonable suspicion. The case reached the Supreme Court on the shadow docket in September 2025; the Court lifted the lower-court injunction restricting race-based stops, drawing dissents calling the ruling a license for blatant racial profiling.

Villegas Molina was first detained by ICE in June 2025 while waiting at a bus stop outside a store in Los Angeles during the LA ICE-raid surge. An immigration judge ordered him released on bond. On April 16, 2026 — months after he became a named plaintiff in the lawsuit — ICE re-detained him without prior notice to him or to his attorneys, despite the standing bond order. He was first held at the B18 ICE facility in the basement of the Los Angeles Metropolitan Detention Center, then transferred to the Adelanto ICE Processing Center in the high desert.

The ACLU of Southern California issued a public statement calling the second detention retaliatory. NDLON attorney Cal Soto said: His arrests were unconstitutional, and his imprisonment in Adelanto was unlawfully cruel and punitive. Civil-rights advocates described it as the first documented retaliatory ICE arrest of a plaintiff challenging immigration raids in the United States. He was released from the Adelanto facility on April 23, 2026 after a week of community pressure, news coverage, and litigation.
profiles.finding: ACLU/NDLON case matches; Getty rally image subject is Jesus R, not assumed Isaac.
profiles.rights: No image accepted; not assumed public domain

profiles.name: Daithí O'Corrain
profiles.description:
Daithí O'Corrain is an Irish peace activist who, on April 11, 2026, broke into Shannon Airport in County Clare, Ireland, and damaged a U.S. military warplane parked there in transit. Shannon Airport has been used as a transit hub by the U.S. military for more than two decades — a long-running source of controversy in Ireland, where the Constitution requires neutrality. He was arrested at the scene and is being held at Limerick Prison (Mulgrave Street, Limerick, V94 P8N1, Ireland), where he is the sole prisoner currently listed on nukeresister.org's 'Inside & Out' page. The action follows a long line of Plowshares-style direct actions at Shannon by Irish peace activists, including the 2003 'Pitstop Ploughshares' case in which five activists damaged a U.S. military aircraft and were ultimately acquitted on a necessity defense.

He secured High Court bail after an initial refusal, and by the May 11, 2026 hearing at Ennis District Court he was on bail awaiting trial — no longer in custody.
profiles.finding: DCU historian namesake excluded; Limerick Post court story is case-specific lead.
profiles.rights: No image accepted; not assumed public domain

profiles.description: Anthony Donovan is a Brooklyn peace activist, musician, and documentary filmmaker whose organizing has included the Catholic Worker movement, Veterans for Peace, Pax Christi International, and the War Resisters League. Donovan was cited and released during an April 1, 2026 blockade at Creech Air Force Base and was arrested for trespass two days later after crossing the Nevada National Security Site boundary during the Sacred Peace Walk.
